title: Canada's Einarson wins 7th Grand Slam of Curling title, 1st since 2024
summary: Kerri Einarson won her seventh Grand Slam of Curling title and first in two years, beating South Korea's Team Kang 6-3 in the women's final at the Co-op Invitational in Victoria on Sunday.

image.caption: Canadian skip Kerri Einarson, pictured at the world championships last March in Calgary. (Jeff McIntosh/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Kerri Einarson won her seventh Grand Slam of Curling title and first in two years, beating South Korea's Team Kang 6-3 in the women's final at the Co-op Invitational in Victoria on Sunday.
New-look rink never trailed en route to 1st Grand Slam title together
Einarson's new-look rink never trailed en route to its first Grand Slam title together. Her team from Gimli, Man., consists of third Shannon Birchard, second Karlee Burgess and lead Jocelyn Peterman.

Team Kang, skipped by Kim Kyeong-ae, tied the game at 2-2 in the third end after Einarson scored singles in the first two, but the five-time Tournament of Hearts champion responded by scoring two with her final shot in the fourth.
Einarson added another deuce in the sixth after holding Kim to a single in the fifth.
Kerri Einarson captures 7th Grand Slam title with victory over Team Kang at Co-op Invitational
Top-ranked Yannick Schwaller of Switzerland will face Norway’s Magnus Ramsfjell in the men’s final later Sunday.

The Co-op Invitational is the first of five stops on a newly compressed Grand Slam of Curling tour that will be completed before Christmas. The next stop is the Masters in Medicine Hat, Alta., from Nov. 3-8.
